title: Make governed MCP tool selection explicit for Codex

requirement.summary: Correct the host guidance and MCP metadata that allowed a fresh Codex Agent to bypass alignment, choose its own development direction, and omit current-Agent self-review during the corrected live replay.

objective.rationale: The native tools are discoverable and executable, but the host needs deterministic repository guidance and intent-oriented tool descriptions to select them at the two product journey boundaries.

goal: Add minimal Codex-visible selection rules and intent-oriented MCP descriptions for alignment before self-selected meaningful development and advisory self-review after resolved work, with deterministic synchronization tests and a fresh installed-runtime replay boundary.
non_goals: Do not force alignment for read-only explanation, diagnosis, status, or a fully specified low-risk request with no material direction choice.
Do not weaken Core validation, fabricate human choices, automatically approve work, or make self-review independent.
Do not change the unrelated no-argument CLI UX change produced during the failed replay.
Do not commit, push, publish, release, deploy, start NYC work, mutate a consumer, or add a second Agent or Provider.
acceptance_signals: Repository instructions tell Codex when meaningful ambiguity requires alignment and prohibit the Agent from selecting the human-owned final direction.
Repository instructions tell the same Agent to run advisory self-review after implementing and validating a human-resolved aligned direction.
The MCP server instructions and start/self-review tool descriptions state the same trigger boundaries without claiming guaranteed model behavior.
Deterministic tests bind repository guidance, server instructions, tool order, descriptions, and privacy/authority limits.
The corrected installed runtime passes a five-tool metadata preflight before any new uncoached replay.
No Git write, publication, release, deployment, NYC work, consumer mutation, second Agent, or independent Reviewer occurs.

items: Over-broad guidance could add governance friction to read-only or fully specified low-risk work.
Tool descriptions influence host selection but cannot guarantee model behavior; only a fresh uncoached replay can supply product evidence.
The dirty working tree contains approved prerequisite and failed-replay changes that must not be mistaken for this correction's scope.

stop_conditions: Stop if the correction requires bypassing host trust, hidden prompt injection, raw conversation retention, or Core weakening.
Stop if instructions let the Agent invent or select the human-owned final direction.
Stop before Git writes, publication, release, deployment, NYC work, consumer mutation, a second Agent, or independent review.

decision.rationale: After reviewing the failed post-correction replay, the user explicitly authorized the proposed tool-selection guidance correction on 2026-08-06.
